reader.requirement: At --std 85, the LINAGE-COUNTER of a sequential file whose FD has LINAGE and EXTERNAL must be one item shared by every program of the run unit that describes that external file, and the LINAGE-COUNTER of a sequential file whose FD has LINAGE and GLOBAL must be referenceable (qualified, or unqualified where unambiguous) from every program directly or indirectly contained in the declaring program, while a non-global file's counter stays invisible to contained programs and a non-external file's counter stays private.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.Has(2014): below 2014 an unqualified LINAGE-COUNTER counts the program's OWN LINAGE files, and with none takes the nearest containing program that declares a GLOBAL LINAGE file; from 2014 the whole visible set counts. Also the edition named in the qualification diagnostic.

reader.edition-search: grep Edition/Has( in CounterResolver.cs, FileControlBinder.FileSection.cs#BindLinageClause and DataBinder.cs; the EXTERNAL sharing rides the external file connector and reads no edition
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: which LINAGE-COUNTER an UNQUALIFIED reference names in a contained program that has LINAGE files of its own (85/2002: its own; 2014+: qualification required when an inherited GLOBAL one is also visible); the qualified reference and the external sharing are the same at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1c11 (accept 85, 2002) covers one level of containment and one external file with an unqualified reference; deeper containment, EXTERNAL plus GLOBAL together, a containee with its own LINAGE file, and the refusal half (a non-global file's counter from a containee, a non-external file of the same name) are not exercised

probes.expected: GLOBAL counter seen and incremented two levels down (C) and seen by A; B's unqualified reference names its own LINAGE file (85 arm); EXTERNAL+GLOBAL counter shared with the separately compiled PXLY and visible unqualified in its containee PXLZ

probes.printed: COBOL0863 LINAGE-COUNTER OF 'NF': the qualifier shall name a file whose file description entry contains a LINAGE clause / COBOL5997 LINAGE-COUNTER referenced, but no file description entry contains a LINAGE clause
probes.expected: a non-GLOBAL file's LINAGE-COUNTER is not visible in a contained program: both references refused
a non-EXTERNAL FD of the same name in another program has its own counter; the external one is untouched

citations.check: OK  §1985:X.4.2.4 GR1  (4.2.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: The counter lives on the file connector, so an EXTERNAL file's single connector gives one counter per run unit and a GLOBAL file's counter follows the file's visibility (VisibleFiles). The refusal of a non-global file's counter in a containee is correct, though COBOL0863's wording ('the qualifier shall name a file whose FD contains a LINAGE clause', citing §2023) says the file lacks LINAGE when the real reason is that it is not visible; a wording point, not a conformance failure.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.8 (qualification) and the 1985 global-name resolution rules (a name declared in program B wins; otherwise the nearest container's global name), plus the 1985 glossary: a contained program is its own source program (terminated by its end program header), so the reader's 85 arm (B's own LINAGE file hides the inherited GLOBAL counter) follows the 1985 text. q5a.cob (runs/q5a-001): A has a GLOBAL LINAGE file GF and a non-global LINAGE file NF; containee B with no LINAGE file references LINAGE-COUNTER unqualified and gets GF's counter (0004 after three WRITEs), since only the global one is in B's set. q5b.cob: two GLOBAL LINAGE files in A, unqualified reference in B: refused COBOL5997. q5c.cob: one GLOBAL and one local LINAGE file, unqualified reference in A itself: refused COBOL5997 (SRL2.8). Citations: OK §1985:X.4.2.4 GR1 (the text is in GR1); OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SRL2.8 (the text is in SRL2.8).
